title: Apple (AAPL) is Westover Capital Advisors LLC’s 2nd Largest Position
text:
Tweet
Westover Capital Advisors LLC raised its stake in Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) by 0.9% in the fourth quarter, according to the company in its most recent filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). The firm owned 34,632 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock after purchasing an additional 325 shares during the period. Apple makes up approximately 3.2% of Westover Capital Advisors LLC’s holdings, making the stock its 2nd biggest position. Westover Capital Advisors LLC’s holdings in Apple were worth $5,861,000 as of its most recent SEC filing.
Other institutional investors also recently modified their holdings of the company. Courier Capital LLC lifted its holdings in shares of Apple by 52.7% during the 3rd quarter. Courier Capital LLC now owns 153,047 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $23,587,000 after acquiring an additional 52,820 shares during the period. Capco Asset Management LLC lifted its holdings in shares of Apple by 1.6% during the 3rd quarter. Capco Asset Management LLC now owns 95,029 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $14,646,000 after acquiring an additional 1,480 shares during the period. HL Financial Services LLC lifted its holdings in shares of Apple by 0.7% during the 3rd quarter. HL Financial Services LLC now owns 1,465,550 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $225,872,000 after acquiring an additional 9,714 shares during the period. Migdal Insurance & Financial Holdings Ltd. lifted its holdings in shares of Apple by 405.4% during the 3rd quarter. Migdal Insurance & Financial Holdings Ltd. now owns 210,249 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $32,404,000 after acquiring an additional 168,650 shares during the period. Finally, Bingham Osborn & Scarborough LLC lifted its holdings in shares of Apple by 10.2% during the 3rd quarter. Bingham Osborn & Scarborough LLC now owns 50,899 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $7,845,000 after acquiring an additional 4,726 shares during the period. 58.13% of the stock is owned by hedge funds and other institutional investors. Shares of Apple opened at $190.80 on Friday, according to MarketBeat . The company has a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.80, a quick ratio of 1.37 and a current ratio of 1.46. Apple has a twelve month low of $142.20 and a twelve month high of $194.20. The company has a market capitalization of $967.61 billion, a price-to-earnings ratio of 20.72, a P/E/G ratio of 1.57 and a beta of 1.29. Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) last announced its quarterly earnings results on Tuesday, May 1st. The iPhone maker reported $2.73 earnings per share for the quarter, beating the Zacks’ consensus estimate of $2.69 by $0.04. Apple had a net margin of 21.55% and a return on equity of 39.97%. The firm had revenue of $61.14 billion for the quarter, compared to analyst estimates of $60.94 billion. During the same quarter in the previous year, the firm posted $2.10 earnings per share. The business’s revenue was up 15.6% on a year-over-year basis. analysts anticipate that Apple will post 11.42 earnings per share for the current year.
The business also recently declared a quarterly dividend, which was paid on Thursday, May 17th. Shareholders of record on Monday, May 14th were paid a $0.73 dividend. The ex-dividend date of this dividend was Friday, May 11th. This represents a $2.92 dividend on an annualized basis and a yield of 1.53%. This is a positive change from Apple’s previous quarterly dividend of $0.63. Apple’s payout ratio is presently 31.70%.
Apple announced that its Board of Directors has approved a share buyback program on Tuesday, May 1st that allows the company to repurchase $100.00 billion in outstanding shares. This repurchase authorization allows the iPhone maker to reacquire up to 11.9% of its shares through open market purchases. Shares repurchase programs are usually an indication that the company’s leadership believes its stock is undervalued.
AAPL has been the subject of several analyst reports. Raymond James reissued a “market perform” rating on shares of Apple in a report on Friday, February 16th. BidaskClub raised shares of Apple from a “sell” rating to a “hold” rating in a report on Saturday, February 17th. Vetr downgraded shares of Apple from a “buy” rating to a “hold” rating and set a $184.49 price target for the company. in a report on Tuesday, February 27th. ValuEngine raised shares of Apple from a “hold” rating to a “buy” rating in a report on Thursday, March 1st. Finally, Rosenblatt Securities set a $180.00 price target on shares of Apple and gave the company a “buy” rating in a report on Wednesday, March 7th. One investment analyst has rated the stock with a sell rating, seventeen have issued a hold rating, thirty-one have given a buy rating and two have assigned a strong buy rating to the stock. The company currently has an average rating of “Buy” and a consensus price target of $205.87.
In other Apple news, insider Philip W. Schiller sold 69,491 shares of Apple stock in a transaction that occurred on Tuesday, April 3rd. The shares were sold at an average price of $166.42, for a total value of $11,564,692.22. The sale was disclosed in a document filed with the SEC, which is available at this hyperlink . Also, SVP Daniel J. Riccio sold 17,375 shares of the business’s stock in a transaction on Wednesday, April 4th. The stock was sold at an average price of $169.12, for a total transaction of $2,938,460.00. Following the completion of the sale, the senior vice president now directly owns 66,191 shares in the company, valued at approximately $11,194,221.92. The disclosure for this sale can be found here . In the last ninety days, insiders sold 272,506 shares of company stock worth $48,367,350. Insiders own 0.08% of the company’s stock.
About Apple
Apple Inc designs, manufactures, and markets mobile communication and media devices, and personal computers to consumers, and small and mid-sized businesses; and education, enterprise, and government customers worldwide. The company also sells related software, services, accessories, networking solutions, and third-party digital content and applications.
